nodes.label: HybridStreamingConfig
nodes.rationale: Configures four-phase adaptive hybrid streaming including the 4-layer defense strategy (new in 0.3.6) protecting against warmup divergence: warm start detection, adaptive step size, cost-increase guard, step clipping.

nodes.label: nlsq.interfaces (docs)
nodes.rationale: Protocol classes enable dependency injection for testing, loose coupling between modules, and clear contracts for implementations.

nodes.label: MemoryPool
nodes.rationale: Size-class bucketing (1KB/10KB/100KB) targets 90% reuse rate and 12.5% peak memory reduction by minimizing malloc/free in hot paths.

nodes.label: Randomized SVD removal (v0.3.5)
nodes.rationale: Randomized SVD (v0.3.1-v0.3.4) was removed because approximation error accumulates across trust-region iterations, causing early termination at worse local minima and 3-25x worse fitting errors. XPCS evidence (50K points, 13 params): full SVD gave 9.74% D0 error in 15 iterations vs randomized SVD 30.18% in 6 iterations.

nodes.label: nlsq.validators module doc
nodes.rationale: Documents nlsq.utils.validators: comprehensive input validation with fast mode and security-focused checks (array size limits, bounds range, parameter validation) to fail fast on malformed input before expensive optimization.

nodes.label: nlsq.workflow module doc
nodes.rationale: Memory-based workflow system. As of v0.5.5 the tier-based system was replaced with a unified memory-budget approach: MemoryBudgetSelector replaces auto_select_workflow() and strategy selection is driven entirely by memory budget computation.

nodes.label: MemoryBudgetSelector
nodes.rationale: Selects strategy by memory analysis: data_gb>threshold -> streaming; peak_gb>threshold -> chunked; else standard.

nodes.label: notebook_utils API reference
nodes.rationale: Notebook transformation utilities using Strategy (transformers) and Chain of Responsibility (pipeline) patterns; idempotent stateless transformers, atomic writes, SHA-256 incremental tracking.

nodes.label: NotebookTransformer
nodes.rationale: Abstract base for transformations (Strategy pattern); stateless, idempotent, pure.

nodes.label: TransformationPipeline
nodes.rationale: Composes transformers with atomic commit and rollback (Chain of Responsibility).

nodes.label: ProcessingTracker
nodes.rationale: Incremental processing via SHA-256 checksums stored in .notebook_transforms.json.

nodes.label: Performance Benchmarks
nodes.rationale: Benchmarks for large-dataset features: 98% memory reduction via dynamic sizing, 20-25x GPU speedup (A100), linear scaling via chunking, unlimited size via streaming. Test on AMD EPYC 7763 / A100 40GB, JAX 0.4.35.

nodes.label: Optimization Case Study: When to Stop Optimizing
nodes.author: Claude Code AI Assistant
nodes.rationale: Profiling revealed JIT compilation (60-75%) and user functions (40%) dominate runtime; only ~40-50ms (8-10%) was optimizable. NumPy<->JAX conversion reduction gave 8% total / 15% core for 1 day effort; lax.scan/vmap/multi-GPU rejected as low ROI (<1%/day) given high complexity cost and already-optimized code.
nodes.norm_label: optimization case study: when to stop optimizing

nodes.label: NLSQ Performance Tuning Guide
nodes.rationale: Reuse CurveFit instances to avoid repeated JIT compilation (10-100x for batch fitting); good initial guesses and bounds speed convergence; lazy imports cut cold start ~43% (1084ms->620ms).

nodes.label: Technical Note: Removal of Randomized SVD (v0.3.5)
nodes.author: NLSQ Development Team
nodes.rationale: Randomized SVD approximation error (~1e-2 to 1e-3) accumulates across trust-region iterations causing convergence to worse minima and early termination (XPCS test: alpha error 24.8x worse). Full deterministic SVD is 3-8x slower but reconstruction error <1e-14 and reproducible; correct trade-off for iterative optimization.
nodes.norm_label: technical note: removal of randomized svd (v0.3.5)

nodes.label: ADR-003: Streaming Optimization Over Subsampling
nodes.author: Wei Chen
nodes.rationale: Subsampling lost scientific accuracy, was non-deterministic, and added ~250 lines of confusing parameters. Streaming processes 100% of data deterministically for ~10-20% runtime overhead; chosen for correctness over speed. Breaking change: enable_sampling/sampling_threshold/max_sampled_size/multistart_subsample_size now raise TypeError.

nodes.label: ADR-004: Parameter Unpacking Simplification
nodes.rationale: 100-line if-elif chain in masked_residual_func existed to avoid early-JAX TracerArrayConversionError. JAX 0.8.0+ handles tuple unpacking efficiently, so replaced with 5-line direct unpacking (func(xdata,*args)): 95% code reduction, 5-10% faster for >10 params, removes artificial 15-param limit.

nodes.label: ADR-005: JAX Autodiff for Gradient Computation
nodes.rationale: Legacy StreamingOptimizer used finite differences requiring O(n_params) function evaluations per gradient with epsilon-tuning errors. Replaced with JAX value_and_grad (single forward+backward pass, cached JIT): 50-100x faster gradients, exact derivatives, scales to 100+ params. Alternatives (manual derivatives, SymPy) rejected for maintenance/performance.
nodes.norm_label: adr-005: jax autodiff for gradient computation

nodes.label: CurveFit God Class (pre-0.6.4)
nodes.rationale: Before v0.6.4 CurveFit was a 2500+ line god class handling validation, detection, bounds, guess, method selection, memory, optimization, and covariance; split into four focused components for testability, debuggability, and extensibility.

nodes.label: Orchestration feature flags (NLSQ_PREPROCESSOR_IMPL)
nodes.rationale: Components toggle between new/legacy impl via env vars for gradual rollout without breaking existing code.

nodes.label: Strategy selection (standard/chunked/streaming)
nodes.rationale: standard when data+Jacobian fit memory (fastest); chunked when Jacobian exceeds memory; streaming when data exceeds memory.

nodes.label: 3-Workflow System (auto / auto_global / hpc)
nodes.rationale: auto: default, optional bounds, fastest; auto_global: multiple minima/unknown guess, bounds required, moderate; hpc: clusters, bounds required.

nodes.label: Parameter bounds (lower/upper arrays)
nodes.rationale: Bounds constrain parameters to physical ranges and define the search space for auto_global; wider bounds = larger search space = slower but more thorough.

nodes.label: sigma / absolute_sigma weighting
nodes.rationale: absolute_sigma=True gives calibrated parameter errors; False (default) scales covariance by residual variance when measurement error is unknown. weight = 1/sigma.

nodes.label: jax.numpy model functions
nodes.rationale: Model functions must use jax.numpy (jnp) not numpy to enable automatic differentiation and GPU acceleration.

nodes.label: popt / pcov return values
nodes.rationale: popt = optimal params; pcov = covariance matrix; perr = sqrt(diag(pcov)); pcov inf means covariance unestimable (poor/ill-conditioned fit).

nodes.label: Linux-only GPU enforcement (JAX_PLATFORM_NAME=cpu on mac/win)
nodes.rationale: GPU acceleration is Linux only; NLSQ forces CPU on macOS/Windows at import time (NLSQ_FORCE_CPU, JAX_PLATFORM_NAME, JAX_PLATFORMS) and adds macOS SIGBUS guards.

nodes.label: Persistent JIT cache (~/.cache/nlsq/jax_cache)
nodes.rationale: First fit includes JIT compilation; subsequent fits ~10x faster via persistent cache.

nodes.label: Multi-GPU n_starts distribution (auto_global/hpc)
nodes.rationale: auto_global/hpc distribute starting points across GPUs; match n_starts to GPU count for even utilization.

nodes.label: macOS GUI stability guards (QT_OPENGL=software, safe mode)
nodes.rationale: macOS guards (software OpenGL, MPLBACKEND=Agg, single-thread XLA, native Qt icons) prevent SIGBUS / text-shaping crashes on Apple Silicon and PySide6 6.10+.
nodes.norm_label: macos gui stability guards (qt_opengl=software, safe mode)

nodes.label: GUI presets (Fast / Robust / Quality)
nodes.rationale: Fast=auto/1e-6; Robust=auto_global/n_starts10/1e-8; Quality=auto_global/n_starts20/1e-10. Presets map to the 3-workflow system.
